back: A dedicated path is set up before communication and its bandwidth is reserved until the end (telephone calls).
A message is split into packets that are routed separately and reassembled in order at the destination (the internet).
Header: addresses, packet number, TTL. Payload: the data. Trailer: end marker and error check.
Guaranteed bandwidth, in-order delivery, constant delay; set-up needed, capacity wasted when idle, lost if a link fails.
Efficient sharing, reroutes around failures; packets may arrive late, out of order or be lost; header overhead.
A router's list of networks and the next hop towards each, with a default route for other addresses.
A count in each packet reduced by 1 at every router; the packet is discarded at 0.
One step of a packet from one router to the next; the hop count is the number of routers passed.
